Photo location guide

Why Is a Located Photo Missing from the Apple Photos Map?

If a photo already shows the correct place in Info, adding GPS again will not explain its map display. This guide focuses on map grouping, the copy or library you are viewing, and checks across devices.

Updated November 4, 2026

First check whether the photo has a locationIf the photo has no locationIf the pin is in the wrong placeIf Info is correct but the map still looks incompleteBatch-fill missing locations after diagnosisVerify the library and export as separate results

First check whether the photo has a location

  1. Find a camera photo that you expected to see on the map and open it directly from the library.
  2. On iPhone, swipe up or tap Info. On Mac, select the photo and press Command-I.
  3. Look for a location and map. If there is none, use the missing-location steps below.
  4. If a map is present, check its pin. A location in the wrong town can make a photo seem absent from the place where you expected it.

Apple Photos places photos on its map using location information. Apple describes that requirement in its Photos map guide. A correct capture date or a place name in your album title does not supply coordinates. A camera photo can therefore be in the library and timeline while having no position on the map.

If the photo has no location

If Info has no place, this is missing GPS rather than a display issue. Use the original-file and transfer checks, then choose a method in the camera-photo location guide. Return here if Info becomes correct but the map remains incomplete.

If the pin is in the wrong place

Correct a saved wrong location with Mac Photos Info or the iPhone adjustment tools. For an unsaved time-matched suggestion, use the clock-offset checks. LensPin never overwrites an existing place.

If Info is correct but the map still looks incomplete

Navigate to the place shown in Info rather than only the place name you originally searched for. Zoom in and out to see whether nearby images are grouped under a thumbnail. Check the full library view as well as any narrower selection you were browsing. Interface labels and map layouts vary by system version.

If you are checking on another device, open the exact same photo there and inspect its information too. Compare the capture time and filename where available. A duplicate, an earlier exported copy or a different library can explain a mismatch without implying that the saved location disappeared. Allow any library synchronization to finish before comparing again.

A useful support report says which photo has the right location in Info, which device or view fails to show it, and whether the same item behaves differently elsewhere. That is more informative than “the map is broken.” Avoid repeatedly editing a correct location merely to refresh the view.

Batch-fill missing locations after diagnosis

Only move to batch matching after confirming the photos have no locations. The method-selection guide explains which clues to use. Adding locations to other photos will not repair the map display of this already located image.

Verify the library and export as separate results

After saving, reopen the image in Apple Photos and inspect its map. LensPin updates the library, not original files. A copy exported earlier will not acquire that change. If you need GPS in EXIF in a new standalone file, export a JPG copy with Include location enabled and inspect that copy separately.

Free download. The first 100 photos/videos located are free. Saving a location to one photo or video counts as one use; skipped and failed items do not count. After that, LensPin Unlimited is an optional one-time purchase, with no subscription. See the App Store for the price in your region.
